description: Reptile and Amphibian Study explores snakes, lizards, turtles, frogs, toads and salamanders: identifying species, how reptiles and amphibians differ, their ecology and protection, venomous species, caring for or observing an animal, field skills, and separating myth from fact.

safety.note: Never handle venomous reptiles, and wash your hands after handling any reptile or amphibian.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words. The 2025 update changed requirement 8. Venomous reptiles may not be used for the animal-care option, and collecting requires permission.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)
